counterfactual_missing_items: Anti-desmoglein serology is not reported, but the intercellular DIF pattern is strongly supportive.
Anti-Ro/Sjögren syndrome antigen A and anti-La/Sjögren syndrome antigen B antibodies are negative, reducing the pure lupus alternative.
No muscle weakness or muscle enzyme evidence is present to support dermatomyositis.
decisive_items: Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes.
abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
Foci of eosinophilic spongiosis in the epidermis.
response.rationale: R1 is best explained by the raw histopathologic and immunofluorescence findings, particularly acantholytic keratinocytes and abundant intercellular IgG/C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis, a pemphigus-class signature. R3 shares photodistribution and ANA positivity with granular BMZ deposits but cannot account for the pemphigus-specific intercellular epidermal deposition and acantholytic/eosinophilic inflammatory pattern. R2 lacks any specific myositis or muscle evidence and has no matching DIF findings.

rejected.why: No myositis, muscle enzyme abnormality, heliotrope/Gottron signs, or matching histologic/DIF findings are provided; ANA positivity and photodistribution alone are nonspecific.

The key raw evidence includes intercellular deposition of IgG/C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis and acantholytic keratinocytes, which are pemphigus-specific rather than lupus-specific; the negative anti-Ro/anti-La/anti-histone and normal complement also weaken pure lupus.
